claims.claim: China's Ministry of Finance and State Taxation Administration announced that from April 1, 2027, the VAT rebate rate for exports of new energy vehicles will be reduced from 13% to 9%.
claims.episode_span: China's decision to cut the VAT export rebate on new energy vehicles from 13 percent to 9 percent starting April 2027
claims.source_title: Tesla sales in China fell 12%, while exports from Shanghai more than doubled — Electrek
claims.supporting_quote: China's Ministry of Finance and State Taxation Administration announced that from April 1, 2027, the VAT rebate rate for exports of new energy vehicles will be reduced from 13% to 9%.

claims.claim: At an average export value of 220,000 yuan the change adds roughly 8,800 yuan per vehicle, which Electrek estimates could cost Tesla around $600 million annually at current export volumes.
claims.episode_span: At an average export value of 220,000 yuan the change adds roughly 8,800 yuan per vehicle, which Electrek estimates could cost Tesla around $600 million annually at current export volumes.
claims.source_title: Tesla sales in China fell 12%, while exports from Shanghai more than doubled — Electrek
claims.supporting_quote: According to Electrek's estimate, with an average export value of a Model 3 or Model Y of around 220,000 yuan, the rebate reduction would mean additional costs of approximately 8,800 yuan per vehicle. The publication estimates the potential annual impact on Tesla at current export rates at about $600 million, but this is not a company estimate.
